notes.meaning: Having a good character and a trusted reputation is worth far more than piles of money. Money can be lost quickly, but a good name brings genuine respect and loving favor from others. We should care much more about living honestly before God than about getting rich.

People from all walks of life share the same basic human dignity because the Lord created every one of them. The wealthy should never look down on the needy, and the poor should not resent the rich. Both need each other in daily life, and both must answer to the same heavenly Father.

A wise and thoughtful person sees trouble coming down the road and takes cover before it strikes. In contrast, people who act carelessly rush straight into danger and suffer painful consequences. Wisdom means paying attention to moral and physical hazards before it is too late to avoid them.

Humility means not being proud, and the fear of the Lord means having deep reverence and respect for God. When someone walks in these virtues, God blesses them with true spiritual riches, lasting honor, and life with Him. The Lord often provides daily necessities and physical protection in this world as well.

People who choose crooked and rebellious ways find that their path is covered with painful thorns and hidden traps. A person who cares about their soul watches their steps carefully and stays far away from those dangerous roads. Staying close to God keeps us safe from unnecessary grief.

Parents and teachers are urged to guide a child in God's ways from their earliest days. Lessons taught with loving discipline take deep root in a young person's heart. These early habits serve as a strong compass that stays with them into old age.

differ.view: Many teach that this verse provides a general principle of wisdom rather than an absolute promise, recognizing that adult children make their own moral choices.
Some hold that this is a dependable divine promise that faithful early instruction will keep a child from departing from the way of life.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars read the phrase according to his way as training tailored to a child's unique gifts and temperament, while others read it as an ironic warning about leaving a child to his own selfish path.

notes.meaning: In this fallen world, having money often gives people power over those who have little. When someone borrows money, they lose much of their freedom and become bound to the lender's demands. Wisdom urges us to be content and avoid the trap of burdensome debt.

Those who plant seeds of unfairness and cruelty will harvest disaster in return. The power they used to hurt and control others will soon be broken by God. In the end, everyone reaps the natural crop of the choices they made.

A generous person looks at the suffering of others with a kind heart and sincere sympathy. Because such a person shares their own food with the hungry, God blesses and enriches them. Showing mercy to the needy always pleases the Lord.

A mocker is someone who ridicules what is good and constantly stirs up trouble. When this bitter, insulting person is removed from a group, the arguments and hurt feelings quickly fade away. Protecting peace often means stepping away from those who refuse to stop quarreling.

A person who loves clean, honest motives and speaks with kind and gracious words earns great respect. Even powerful rulers value advisers who are truthful rather than those who only flatter them. True inner goodness makes someone a trustworthy friend in any company.

The Lord actively watches over true knowledge and protects those who speak His truth. At the same time, He ruins the plans and treacherous words of dishonest people. God ensures that the truth will outlast every human lie.

A lazy person invents wild and ridiculous excuses just to avoid going outside to work. He claims there is a roaring lion loose in the public square, hoping that imaginary danger will let him stay in bed. Laziness makes people dream up reasons to run away from their daily duties.

The seductive, flattering words of an immoral person are like a deep pit dug to trap wild animals. Falling into sexual sin leads to spiritual and moral ruin that is very hard to climb out of. Those who turn away from God's commands often find themselves trapped in the consequences of their lust.

A natural bent toward foolish rebellion is present in the heart of every child from birth. Gentle words alone are not always enough, so firm and loving discipline is needed to guide them in the right direction. Proper correction helps drive away stubborn foolishness so wisdom can take its place.

Trying to get rich by mistreating the poor or by flattering the wealthy with expensive gifts leads straight to poverty. God opposes dishonest gain, and ill-gotten wealth soon disappears. Greed and selfish schemes never produce lasting prosperity.

This marks the start of a special collection of teachings that requires our full attention. The speaker asks the reader to lean forward, listen closely, and take these wise instructions to heart. Learning wisdom requires a humble and willing mind.

Holding wise sayings deep in your thoughts brings great inner delight and peace. When these truths are stored in your heart, they will also be ready on your lips whenever you speak. Wisdom on the inside leads to helpful and encouraging words for those around us.

The main purpose of all true biblical wisdom is to teach a person to put their complete trust in the Lord. The teacher speaks directly to the individual student, making the lessons personal and vital for today. Wisdom is not just clever life advice; it is a path to relying on God.

The writer reminds his student that he has provided a valuable set of thirty sayings full of sound advice and true understanding. These lessons were written down so that anyone could read and remember how to live well. God has provided clear guidance so we do not have to wander in confusion.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Scholars widely connect this reference to thirty sayings with the ancient Egyptian Instruction of Amenemope, which shares thirty chapters of similar counsel adapted here to honor the Lord.

notes.meaning: These instructions are given so the student can be certain about what is genuinely true and reliable. By learning sound wisdom, he will be prepared to give accurate, truthful answers to those who send him on official business. Knowing God's truth equips us to speak with honesty and confidence.

We are strictly warned never to rob poor people simply because they lack the power to defend themselves, nor to deny them justice in legal courts. The Lord Himself acts as their personal defender and takes up their legal battle. Anyone who steals from the helpless will face God's severe judgment.

A wise person does not build close friendships with someone who is constantly angry or hot-tempered. Bad habits spread quickly, and spending time with a furious person will tempt you to copy their uncontrolled rage. Choosing calm and patient friends protects your soul from deadly traps.

It is foolish to shake hands and promise to pay back loans made by someone else. If that person fails to pay and you have no money to spare, the creditor can come and take away your very bed. Wisdom tells us not to gamble our family's basic needs on another person's debts.

In ancient Israel, stone markers were set up to show the legal boundaries between family properties. Moving those markers was a form of sneaky theft that stole land from your neighbor. God commands us to respect other people's property rights and live with strict honesty.

A worker who masters their trade and carries out their job with skill and diligence will surely rise. Instead of remaining unnoticed in the service of obscure employers, their hard work will earn them a place before kings. Faithful, high-quality work brings honor and opens doors to serve in great ways.
